body:
Follow-up to closed #2668 / merged #2727. This is a distinct asymmetric Git-header witness, not a reopening of the delivered ordinary rename claim.

## Identity and ownership

Evidence and local candidate owner: the delegated Codex CLI diff-selection session from parent source thread `01a0f5ca-1f3e-7133-89f1-64b544b500c0`. The authorized continuation produced one isolated, unpublished local repair on branch `codex/7795-mixed-quote`, worktree `/workspace/ripr-7795`. Exact candidate commit `fbfe9ebab2375776ddd6a1a7db745191b53c8409`, tree `7a6e54d63e5c13e6beda918257516929e5a8ae79`, saved parent `3480fb20aae5d30df95a956e9683dfe7be0c1e18`. No same-claim active header writer was identified in the available ownership evidence. Acceptance remains the five predicates below. Latest-main identity/reproduction, publication, hosted proof and protected integration remain unresolved; denied reads stay stopped.

Executed repository/source: `EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm`, saved branch `work`, commit `3480fb20aae5d30df95a956e9683dfe7be0c1e18`, tree `5a448c1048cba7a879a8de698d004284e49fe080`. This is the immutable pre-repair baseline; original checkout remains clean. Linux x86_64; Rust 1.95.0; locked, serial build with only `lang-rust` (`--no-default-features --features lang-rust`). Cargo originally selected absolute executable `/workspace/diff-selection-target/debug/ripr`; frozen baseline is now `/workspace/diff-selection-proof/bin/base-3480fb20-ripr` (the Cargo target has since been reused). Baseline SHA256 `9e546be5261636e83c818a51794c3d13ee247441adb3a9605b4225879e1d9d46`; build finished success in 3m07s. Cargo.lock SHA256 `dc7d4697e595b3f2fd26d0705430136684e1fc64f91f959f676d3ec5ad7b79b6`.

First observation: 2026-10-13T23:57:17Z; follow-up proof completed before this issue's 2026-10-14T00:02:39Z creation. Premise status: **NEEDS_FRESH_EVIDENCE for latest main; reproduced on exact saved source**. The saved checkout has no `origin/main`; shell action `gh api repos/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/commits/main` returned `Forbidden`. That action was stopped without retry/bypass. This issue does not claim the newest main reproduces.

## Executed behavior

A real Git R100 rename `src/lib.rs -> src/日本語.rs` gives this normal Git header with `core.quotePath=true`:

```text
diff --git a/src/lib.rs "b/src/\346\227\245\346\234\254\350\252\236.rs"
similarity index 100%
rename from src/lib.rs
rename to "src/\346\227\245\346\234\254\350\252\236.rs"
```

The fixture also updates Cargo.toml's `[lib] path` to the new name, so the target remains valid. Independent `git diff --name-status -z main...HEAD` reports `M\0Cargo.toml\0R100\0src/lib.rs\0src/日本語.rs\0`.

Actual `ripr check --base main --json`:
- exit 0; `analysis_complete: true`; `no_behavioral_candidates`;
- changed_file_count 1, changed_line_count 2: only the Cargo.toml edit;
- zero probes, zero findings, zero changed Rust files;
- stderr says only one non-source `.toml` file was found. No rename notice. The renamed source vanished from scope.

With an actual R095 rename plus the literal predicate change `amount >= threshold -> amount > threshold`, the same mixed header loses the rename/old-path-association notice, while correctly producing two findings (predicate and return_value) at `./src/日本語.rs:2`, owner `changed`, expression `amount > threshold`.

Isolating the valid quoted pure-rename section via `--diff` yields exit 2, `unsupported_input`, limitation `malformed_diff`, and advice to provide a valid unified diff. Thus the isolated form fails closed but its diagnosis is wrong; a separately parseable Cargo.toml section masks the missing rename and produces a complete-looking result.

Controls: both paths unquoted (including spaces), old path quoted only, and both paths quoted each retain the correct notice in pure and edited cases: **6/6 controls**. New path quoted only reproduces both defects: **2/2 witnesses**. Expected filenames/operators are literal pins checked against native NUL Git inventories, not values derived from RIPR's parser.

## Source inference (distinct from executed CLI proof)

[`analysis/diff/path.rs::parse_git_old_path`](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/3480fb20aae5d30df95a956e9683dfe7be0c1e18/crates/ripr/src/analysis/diff/path.rs#L19) takes an unquoted old header through `split_once(" b/")`. A quoted destination begins ` "b/`, so this produces no old path. [`parse.rs::handle_rename_metadata`](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/3480fb20aae5d30df95a956e9683dfe7be0c1e18/crates/ripr/src/analysis/diff/parse.rs#L402) requires `section_old_path` to equal the rename-from path before counting a rename. This explains the directional matrix. The function-level cause is source inference; the CLI outputs above were executed.

## Local candidate and executed proof

Only the production old-path reader changes: it recognizes the independently quoted destination boundary before its existing unquoted boundary. The existing metadata/disclosure consumers, native decoder/confinement, exact rename-from match, and loader quoting pin are reused. Five files changed (188 insertions, 1 deletion): reader, parser rejection controls, real-Git CLI regression, three RIPR-SPEC-0170 traceability symbols and a canonical Fixed changelog fragment. No workflow, dependency, schema, message or support-tier change.

Exact-head frozen Rust-only executable: `/workspace/diff-selection-proof/bin/candidate-fbfe9eba-ripr`, SHA256 `f2d935ef1aedf3d078718572e1c54ff963b143119c746cb129eaacbccdd30e28`. Distinct default-feature executable: `/workspace/diff-selection-proof/bin/default-fbfe9eba-ripr`, SHA256 `f0e1bb3e3c05baca6f261c1ac04a4a3f49800768efff3547e266fd6148a5cf8d`. Both have terminal Cargo artifact/source identity receipts in `candidate/green-identity.json` and `candidate/default-identity.json`.

Executed Linux proof, exact commit above:

- Qualified pre-repair regression: one selected test, native exit 101, intended missing notice/scope assertion. Earlier zero-test selector output remains an excluded instrument failure.
- Candidate CLI selection: 2 passed, 0 ignored; the new real-Git test covers five literal path layouts × pure/edited with native NUL inventories, committed/worktree selection and isolated pure sections. Existing control-byte/source-selection regression also passes.
- Path units: 20 passed, 0 ignored. Diff parser units: 78 passed, 0 ignored. New traversal and nearby old-name mismatch controls remain rejected.
- Independent alternate frozen-binary oracle: candidate **14/14**, baseline **4/14**. All ten positive baseline cases fail the intended behavior. Alternate controls cover CRLF, native invalid-byte versus literal octal mimic identity, a file-budget refusal, section identity reset, confinement, and an actual Git R098 rename to a native TAB filename with differing committed/live predicates. Native TAB provenance is confirmed from retained NUL inventory and output bytes. The loader's unchanged quote pin is established by source inspection; TAB quoting alone cannot discriminate that pin.
- Prepared default-feature goldens: **405 subjects, 996 output comparisons, zero drift**. Advisory dogfood passes. All 9 source-policy gates, traceability, changelog-fragment check and default-feature production-library Clippy pass. Library Clippy and selected tests do not establish all-target/workspace proof.
- Initial goldens failed with three semantic `exposed -> weakly_exposed` surfaces for the existing locked fixture. This failure is retained, not blessed or relabeled. The existing workflow prerequisite and #7616 require `cargo fetch --locked --manifest-path fixtures/owner_return_pin_fallible_literal/input/Cargo.toml`. With unchanged frozen binaries/source and fresh caches, baseline and candidate both show weakly_exposed before preparation and exposed afterward. Baseline is Rust-only and candidate has default features: this is an availability discriminator for the same Rust fixture, not a full default-feature baseline matrix.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and exact-base `git diff --check` pass. `precommit` exits 1 with `incomplete_evidence`; `check-fast` exits 1 before gates because the saved Git store lacks `origin/main` and `main`. No fake refs were created. Full workspace matrix, native Windows/macOS and hosted proof remain unexecuted.

Independent exact-head review: `/workspace/diff-selection-proof/review/exact-head-review.json`, no actionable candidate findings, overall **REVIEW_INCOMPLETE**. Missing current-source, selectors, full matrix, hosted and integration/publication evidence prevent a readiness claim. The review read primary terminal receipts and executed different adversarial fixtures; it did not rerun Cargo or read denied GitHub targets.

Inherited residual, outside this candidate's claim: both-unquoted real Git old name containing ` b/` still yields an isolated malformed-diff result on both frozen baseline and candidate (same fallback delimiter). Original native inventory, diff and both outputs are retained under `review/inherited-unquoted-*`. A future owner should first reconcile current same-claim work and independently qualify that separate boundary; this repair does not represent it as fixed.

Serial Cargo admission: 8 GiB incremental disk ceiling with 20 GiB free reserve, 8 GiB child memory budget and 600-second command bound. Observed largest child RSS 6,927,760 KiB; longest command 507.84 seconds. Build sessions are terminal. Retained local worktree, unique frozen executables, raw negatives and reusable tool/cache state are identified in `candidate/closeout.json`. Reviewable unpublished PR body: `candidate/pr-body.md`. No branch push, PR publication, hosted CI, protected merge, package/release or deployment was performed.

## Executed bounded fallback

For the verified **UTF-8** paths in these fixtures, generate a supplied diff outside the fixture and pass it to the existing CLI route:

```bash
git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ --submodule=short --unified=0 main...HEAD > /tmp/ripr-rename.diff
ripr check --diff /tmp/ripr-rename.diff --json
```

Both runs exit 0. Pure: zero probes with the explicit pure-rename/no-probes notice. Edited: the same two literal new-path findings and the old-path associations-not-carried-forward notice. Actual fallback diff SHA256: pure `01de5fa41769e8a4631cd0ffe5c668fe2e1bd86d5d23995a37c4539f7ea08e22`; edited `e7212e5d91949dc1233383c1b215cccac0d4e759cf4159936aa50184a447f036`. This is a consumer workaround, **not** a suggestion to remove the loader's byte-identity quoting pin, and not qualified for invalid-byte filenames.

## Acceptance and next action

Current owner: this Codex session's local candidate, handed back to the parent delivery owner with exact receipts. Next action: acquire a newly authorized current-source basis, reconcile latest substantive same-claim decisions, and reproduce the witness before publishing a draft PR. If the boundary still needs this candidate, complete normal required qualification and published-head review; request ordinary hosted CI when expected green and carry it through protected integration. Do not retry or route around the denied reads. No issue acceptance or RIPR 0.11 readiness is declared.

Acceptance:
1. Literal, native-inventory controls cover all four old/new quoting combinations, pure and edited.
2. A pure mixed-quote rename is counted/disclosed without invented probes or a malformed-diff accusation; an adjacent parseable file cannot conceal it.
3. Edited mixed-quote findings retain the new path, line 2, actual live/committed expression and the existing old-path-association limitation.
4. Existing confinement/adversarial path controls remain fail-closed. Do not remove `core.quotePath=true` globally or relabel wrong goldens.
5. Meaningful pre-repair red, candidate green, independent exact-head review and ordinary required hosted CI precede protected integration.

Non-goals: test-association transfer, new parser architecture, Python/TypeScript oracle changes, gate/policy/MCP/SDLC changes, releases, deployment, credentials/settings/permission changes, or runner allocation.

Ownership reconciliation: current #2668 and all three comments read; #2727 is merged. Finding-specific all-state searches for `parse_git_old_path`, quoted/Unicode rename, and mixed quoting found no same-claim active candidate. #4006 concerns NUL path inventories, not this unified-diff header pairing; no overlapping source scope was edited.

Retained exact receipts in this saved environment: `/workspace/diff-selection-proof/identity.json`, `build.jsonl`, first-run `commands.json`/`results.json`, `followup/rename-observations.json`, `followup/fallback-records.json`, and complete producer/consumer stdout/stderr. First-run failures remain intact. The unrelated untracked fixture initially had an invalid compiled-subject expectation: RIPR correctly returned a named module-tree limitation. A declared-module native-compile control verifies intent-to-add changes 0 findings to 2, and executing the orphan's module-declaration recovery yields the same two subject findings plus one conservative `static_unknown` declaration finding; those are not counted as source defects.
title: ux(diff): ASCII-to-Unicode rename loses disclosure; adjacent file masks missing scope
